source: Liu et al. (2021) What Makes Good In-Context Examples for GPT-3? (KATE)
finding: Picking in-context examples by nearest-neighbour similarity in a sentence-embedding space beats random picking for GPT-3.
numbers: IMDB sentiment accuracy: random 87.95 +/-2.74; KATE-roberta 91.99; KATE-sst2 93.43. NQ: random 28.6, KATE-nli 40.8 to 41.6. WQ: random 41.0, KATE up to 50.6. TriviaQA: random 59.2, KATE up to 62.4.
limits: GPT-3 only; 100 sampled test questions on NQ; random baseline has a 3-point spread across draws.
agent_relevance: Nearest-case retrieval is a strong default over random memory when the pool is big.

source: Liu et al. (2021) What Makes Good In-Context Examples for GPT-3? (KATE)
finding: The encoder used for similarity matters: an encoder tuned on a similar task helps, one tuned on a dissimilar task hurts.
numbers: IMDB: KATE-roberta 91.99, KATE-nli 90.40, KATE-nli+sts-b 90.20, KATE-sst2 93.43. Plain kNN-roberta (retrieved neighbours' labels used directly, no GPT-3) 50.20, near chance.
limits: Task-matched fine-tuning tested on sentiment only.
agent_relevance: The similarity metric must match the task goal. Generic semantic distance is not enough for a problem-solving memory.

source: Liu et al. (2021) What Makes Good In-Context Examples for GPT-3? (KATE)
finding: KATE beats random even with 5 examples; the gain shrinks when the retrieval pool is small.
numbers: NQ: KATE beats random for k from 5 up; paper varies training pool from 1k to about 70k and reports larger pool gives larger gain.
limits: Two datasets (NQ, WQ). Example order also changes results.
agent_relevance: A library of solved subgoals needs enough size before retrieval pays off.

source: Rubin, Herzig, Berant (2022) Learning To Retrieve Prompts for In-Context Learning (EPR)
finding: BM25 (word overlap) beat SBERT (dense) as unsupervised retriever for structured outputs. A retriever trained on LM-scored positives (EPR) beat both.
numbers: Dev, GPT-Neo, BREAK/MTOP/SMCalFlow: RANDOM 1.7/7.3/8.9; SBERT 21.6/48.7/43.6; BM25 26.0/52.9/46.1; CBR baseline 25.7/57.0/51.4; EPR 31.9/64.2/54.3.
limits: Semantic parsing only; 1,000-example dev subsamples for GPT-3/Codex; one run per cell.
agent_relevance: Surface overlap can beat embedding similarity. Plain similarity is not the best proxy for usefulness.

source: Rubin, Herzig, Berant (2022) Learning To Retrieve Prompts for In-Context Learning (EPR)
finding: There is a big gap between what simple similarity retrieves and what would help the LM (oracle upper bounds).
numbers: BREAK dev: BM25 26.0, EPR 31.9, BM25-ORACLE (retrieve by gold output) 32.3, LM-ORACLE 43.1; one-shot ANYCORRECT-ORACLE 53.6. Test GPT-Neo BREAK/MTOP: BM25 17.6/49.0, CBR 18.4/57.5, EPR 23.9/64.4.
limits: Oracles use gold labels, so cannot be used at test time.
agent_relevance: Case utility for the solver differs from case similarity. Outcome feedback (as in b14) can close part of the gap.

source: Rubin, Herzig, Berant (2022) Learning To Retrieve Prompts for In-Context Learning (EPR)
finding: EPR even beat the BM25 gold-output oracle on two datasets, so output similarity is not an upper bound on utility.
numbers: MTOP: EPR 64.2 vs BM25-ORACLE 58.9. SMCalFlow: 54.3 vs 47.3. BREAK: 31.9 vs 32.3 (tie).
limits: Dev results, one scoring LM.
agent_relevance: Supports learning retrieval from outcomes, not from similarity alone.

source: Kapuriya, Kaushik, Ganguly, Bhatia (2025) Exploring the Role of Diversity in Example Selection for In-Context Learning (SIGIR)
finding: Re-ranking top retrieved examples with maximal marginal relevance (MMR) improves or keeps F1 in most settings, so pure nearest-neighbour is redundant.
numbers: Paper says MMR beats or matches standard ICL in about 70% of configurations. COLA SBERT-MMR up to +9.7%; RTE TFIDF-MMR +2.7%; SST2 gains 0.0 to 1.2%.
limits: Small LMs (Phi-2, Mistral, LLaMA), classification (RTE, COLA, SST2, TREC). Gains tiny on easy tasks.
agent_relevance: Add a diversity term to retrieval but expect little gain on easy, well-separated tasks.

source: Kapuriya, Kaushik, Ganguly, Bhatia (2025) Exploring the Role of Diversity in Example Selection for In-Context Learning (SIGIR)
finding: Best MMR weight is usually lambda 0.5 or higher; benefit depends on lexical vs dense similarity and on model size.
numbers: Best lambda mostly >= 0.5; SBERT-MMR better on COLA; TFIDF-MMR better with larger models on TREC.
limits: Lambda tuned per dataset on the evaluated grid, so gains are optimistic.
agent_relevance: Tune the similarity-diversity weight on held-out tasks, not the test.

source: Xiao, Zhao, Huang (2025) The Role of Diversity in In-Context Learning for LLMs
finding: Pure similarity (TopK) is best on easy tasks; diversity (TopK-Div) helps on harder tasks (reading, SQL, multi-step math, GeoQuery).
numbers: Llama-3.1-8B, k=4: SST-2 TopK 94.13 vs TopK-Div 92.75 vs Div 91.50. SQuAD TopK 73.28 vs TopK-Div 77.71. CsQA TopK 72.57 vs TopK-Div 72.77. Text: GeoQuery TopK-Div at least +7 points absolute over TopK.
limits: Three families (Llama-3.1, Gemma-2, Mistral-v0.3); k=4 and 8; ten permutations for TopK; std under 1% in most cells. Table read from extracted text, so row alignment for some cells was ambiguous.
agent_relevance: Task difficulty is a moderator: similarity for routine subgoals, add diversity for novel ones.

source: Xiao, Zhao, Huang (2025) The Role of Diversity in In-Context Learning for LLMs
finding: Random selection beat TopK on math and reading where the model already has strong zero-shot skill. Authors hypothesise diversity points the model to general skills rather than coverage.
numbers: Llama-3.1-8B GSM8K k=4: Rand 81.99, TopK 81.74, Div 82.81, TopK-Div 82.98. Too much diversity (Rand, Div) hurts GeoQuery.
limits: GSM8K gaps are about 1 point. The explanation is a hypothesis, not tested.
agent_relevance: Similar-case retrieval can anchor a strong model on a wrong pattern; mix in a different case.

source: Xiao, Zhao, Huang (2025) The Role of Diversity in In-Context Learning for LLMs
finding: Diversity-aware selection also improves robustness to out-of-distribution queries (stated in abstract and Amazon-review test).
numbers: Paper reports TopK-Div beats TopK when demonstrations come from a shifted domain (Amazon); exact margin not recorded.
limits: Margin not extracted.
agent_relevance: If queries drift from the library, similarity retrieval degrades; diversity buffers it.

source: Min et al. (2022) Rethinking the Role of Demonstrations: What Makes In-Context Learning Work?
finding: Replacing demonstration labels with random labels barely hurts. A retrieved case helps partly by its format, label space and input distribution, not only its right answer.
numbers: 12 models incl. GPT-3: drop 0 to 5% absolute; mean drop 2.6% in classification, 1.7% in multi-choice.
limits: Classification and multi-choice with models up to GPT-3; not tested on multi-step reasoning. Later large models may read labels more.
agent_relevance: Do not assume the stored solution content is what helps. Test with corrupted cases.

source: Sarukkai, Xie, Fatahalian (2025) Self-Generated In-Context Examples Improve LLM Agents for Sequential Decision-Making
finding: A growing database of the agent's own successful trajectories, retrieved by cosine similarity, raises success rate without training.
numbers: ALFWorld 73% to 89%; Wordcraft 55% to 64%; InterCode-SQL 75% to 79% (gpt-4o-mini). Gains exceed upgrading gpt-4o-mini to gpt-4o and match allowing multiple attempts per task.
limits: Three benchmarks; naive accumulation varies across five trials.
agent_relevance: Direct evidence for a case library of own solved subgoals retrieved by similarity.

source: Sarukkai, Xie, Fatahalian (2025) Self-Generated In-Context Examples Improve LLM Agents for Sequential Decision-Making
finding: Naive accumulation is unstable; curating the database (population-based) and exemplars by retrieval-weighted utility lifts results further.
numbers: ALFWorld reaches 93% with database-level and exemplar-level curation, above methods that use stronger LLMs and hand-made parts.
limits: Some of five trial databases did worse than others; retrieval uses averaged cosine over goal, plan and observation keys.
agent_relevance: Keep a utility score per case from retrieval outcomes as the retention rule.

source: Sarukkai, Xie, Fatahalian (2025) Self-Generated In-Context Examples Improve LLM Agents for Sequential Decision-Making
finding: Marginal value of each new stored example falls as the database grows.
numbers: Authors report efficiency declines because each new example is retrieved less often.
limits: Qualitative statement.
agent_relevance: Cap the library; add only cases that cover new regions.

source: Shi et al. (2023) Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context
finding: One irrelevant sentence added to a math problem sharply lowers accuracy. Retrieved text that is similar but off-target is a risk.
numbers: Of base problems solved by greedy decoding, no more than 18% were solved for all distractor types; fewer than 30% consistently solved after distractors; role-overlap distractors drove one model's macro accuracy to 0.
limits: GSM-IC with code-davinci-002 and text-davinci-003; older models.
agent_relevance: Retrieval returning near-misses can hurt. Filter retrieved cases and show only the relevant part.

source: Shi et al. (2023) Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context
finding: Self-consistency recovers most of the loss, so the model can still reach the answer but is unreliable on one try.
numbers: Recall of the correct answer 99.7% with 20 samples on GSM-IC.
limits: Recall of any correct sample, not majority-vote accuracy.
agent_relevance: Sampling helps, but under G4 agreement is only a hint; verify with a check.

source: Liu et al. (2023) Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
finding: Accuracy depends on where the relevant document sits: best at start or end, worst in the middle.
numbers: GPT-3.5-Turbo multi-document QA can drop by over 20%; at 20 and 30 documents worst case falls below closed-book 56.1%. Adding retrieved context helped only 1.5% (GPT-3.5) and 1% (Claude-1.3) over a best-case reader setup.
limits: 2023 models; newer long-context models may be flatter.
agent_relevance: Put the best-matched case first or last; do not stuff many cases into the middle.

source: Liu et al. (2023) Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
finding: Longer-context versions of the same model did not read the middle better.
numbers: GPT-3.5-Turbo 56.1 (4K) vs 56.0 (16K); Claude-1.3 48.3 vs 48.2 (100K) in the closed-book/oracle comparison table.
limits: Table columns read from extracted text.
agent_relevance: More context length does not fix retrieval ordering; fewer, better cases.

source: Thakur et al. (2021) BEIR: A Heterogeneous Benchmark for Zero-shot Evaluation of IR Models
finding: On 18 zero-shot retrieval datasets BM25 is a robust baseline that dense retrievers often fail to beat out of domain. Re-ranking works best.
numbers: BM25+cross-encoder beats BM25 on 16 of 18 datasets; ColBERT beats BM25 on 9 of 18; dense and sparse models often underperform. Metric nDCG@10.
limits: Document retrieval, not case retrieval; 2021 models.
agent_relevance: Use lexical plus dense retrieval, then rerank. Do not trust dense embeddings alone on new domains.

source: Wiratunga et al. (2024) CBR-RAG: Case-Based Reasoning for Retrieval Augmented Generation in LLMs for Legal QA
finding: Hybrid case retrieval combining embeddings of case parts beat a no-retrieval baseline and a single-embedding variant, by a small margin.
numbers: Best: hybrid AnglEBERT weights [0.25,0.40,0.35], k=3: +1.94% mean cosine similarity over No-RAG; significant at 95% vs No-RAG and vs hybrid LegalBERT k=3 (one-tailed t-test); full case in prompt beat support text only.
limits: Legal QA only; metric is semantic similarity of answer, not correctness; No-RAG baseline already high.
agent_relevance: Match on several case parts (problem, plan, outcome), not one embedding.

source: Memento (2025) Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs
finding: A case bank with similarity retrieval gives a small in-distribution gain over no case memory; a learned Q-function retriever gives more.
numbers: DeepResearcher PM% over iterations 1 to 5: no CBR 78.65, 80.93, 82.62, 83.53, 84.47; non-parametric CBR 79.84, 81.87, 83.09, 84.03, 84.85; parametric CBR 80.46, 82.84, 84.10, 84.85, 85.44. Out-of-distribution gain 4.7 to 9.6 points.
limits: In-distribution gain at iteration 5 only 0.4 (non-parametric) and 1.0 (parametric); case bank saturates at about 3k items.
agent_relevance: Learned case value beats raw similarity, as in EPR. Gain is larger out-of-distribution.

source: Ye et al. (2023) Compositional Exemplars for In-context Learning (CEIL)
finding: Choosing the example set jointly (determinantal point process trained on LM feedback) beats choosing examples one by one by similarity, including EPR in most cases.
numbers: Paper reports CEIL substantially outperforms learning-free TopK-BERT, mostly outperforms EPR, and gains up to 45% absolute over random in one setting.
limits: Per-task numbers not recorded this session.
agent_relevance: Treat selection as a set problem (relevance plus coverage), not a ranked list.

source: Synthesis across b01, b04, b13, b22: similarity vs learned utility
finding: Raw similarity beats random by several to 12+ points; learned or outcome-weighted retrieval adds more; diversity helps on hard tasks only. No meta-analysis pooling these exists.
numbers: KATE vs random +4 (IMDB), +12 (NQ); EPR vs BM25 +5.9 (BREAK dev), +11.3 (MTOP dev); Memento parametric vs non-parametric +0.6 at iteration 5.
limits: Different models, tasks and metrics; my own comparison, not a statistical pooling.
agent_relevance: Order of use: similarity first, then outcome weights, then diversity for novel problems.

source: Synthesis across b07, b09, b12, b20, b22: null and weak results
finding: Several results limit the claim that similar cases help: easy tasks gain nothing from diversity, random labels cost under 5%, dense loses to BM25 out of domain, small case banks saturate.
numbers: SST-2 diversity gain 0.0 to 1.2%; Min random-label drop 0 to 5%; Memento in-distribution gain under 1 point.
limits: No direct replication of KATE found in the papers opened this session.
agent_relevance: Ablate with random and wrong-answer cases before trusting the library.
